observation_summary: The bug report and failing tests confirm that DateTimeFormatter.parseInto overwrites the year of the target instant with a default year (2000) when parsing formats that do not include a year. The fix involves passing the instant's current year to the DateTimeParserBucket instead of the hardcoded default.
hypothesis: The DateTimeFormatter.parseInto method incorrectly uses a hardcoded default year (iDefaultYear) when parsing date strings that lack year information, instead of using the year from the provided instant.
prediction: The DateTimeParserBucket constructor in DateTimeFormatter is being initialized with iDefaultYear, which overrides the existing year in the target instant. Changing this to use the year from the instant itself will resolve the issue.
experiment_rationale: The provided fix diff clearly shows that the constructor call for DateTimeParserBucket was changed from using iDefaultYear to using chrono.year().get(instantLocal). This is a classic initialization error where the wrong value is used to initialize the state of the parser bucket.
reasoning_summary: The bug is an incorrect initialization of the DateTimeParserBucket. The code was using a fixed default year instead of the year derived from the input instant, leading to incorrect date calculations when the year was missing from the input string.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not a change in the procedural logic or algorithm, but rather a change in the value used to initialize the parser bucket.
There is no missing guard or validation logic; the issue is the value being passed to the constructor.
